rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: The current report was published on 14 July 2026 and covers 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: ORR describes overall outcomes as broadly stable while judging that risk control and assurance are not yet at the required level; this is a regulator assessment rather than a parcel metric.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: RM3 assessments identified performance differences across Network Rail regions and functions, including asset management and safe-system implementation.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: A programme of structural assessments improved understanding and assurance of asset risks.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: Track-worker safety remains a key concern and the Radlett fatal incident is cited as evidence that planned protections are not always delivered.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: ORR reports increased level-crossing risk and rising fatalities, indicating controls are not consistently achieving intended outcomes.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: The Shap derailment is used to underline infrastructure-management needs under environmental pressure and changing asset conditions.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: Overspeeding remains a significant and insufficiently controlled railway risk.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: ORR highlights violence, harassment, fatigue management and welfare provision as workforce risks requiring a systematic response.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: The Freight Safe Wagon Condition Programme is identified as an example of coordinated risk-management improvement.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: Non-mainline safety is described as broadly stable, with differences in management maturity and risk-control capability.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: TfL governance is generally strong, while operational delivery remains uneven for ageing assets, platform-train interfaces and occupational health.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: Serious tram incidents remain rare, but weaknesses persist in public-interface risk management.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: Heritage railways' reliance on individual competence and experience can limit organisational resilience.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: ORR reports work on train-driver licensing modernisation, ROGS review and railway standards improvement.

rows.source: ORR Annual health and safety report 2025-26
rows.verified: The regulator delivered inspections, approvals and enforcement activity to address risk and secure compliance.
ORR combines actual harm, modelled risk, RM3 assessments, inspection evidence, near misses, asset performance and safety-culture intelligence.
ORR states that April 2025 to March 2026 safety statistics will be published separately in September 2026; the future statistical release must not be inferred from the annual assessment.
